teams.heading: Jake White's Fiji edge Japan 34-28 in Tokyo for winning start
teams.body: Jake White's Fiji edged Eddie Jones' Japan 34-28 in Tokyo on Saturday, a winning start to the coach's tenure. Ben Volavola, a substitute, kicked two penalties after the break to decide a roller-coaster game in the rain. White picked no Europe-based players and handed out four new caps, saying Fiji "can beat anyone" on their day before the Nations Championship games against France, Ireland and Italy.

lead.why: A new result from the men's Test side, with Jake White's first game in charge, outranks the older background pieces already on the tab.

teams.heading: Borthwick could call up Barton, Jibulu and Hicks in November
teams.body: Steve Borthwick could turn to uncapped players in November, with Planet Rugby's list headed by Gloucester full-back George Barton, whose form is pushing him into the picture. Sale hooker Nathan Jibulu, 23, has two man-of-the-match awards this season and is seen as a long-term option as Jamie George nears the end of his Test career. Max Hicks, a New Zealand-born back-rower who qualifies through ancestry, has impressed for Newcastle Red Bulls in his first PREM season.

lead.why: The only new England men's Test-squad item in the shortlist, covering uncapped options for the November Nations Championship window.

teams.heading: Galthié names South African-born Jeremy Ward in France squad amid injury crisis
teams.body: Fabien Galthié has called up Stade Français's Jeremy Ward, a 30-year-old former Junior Springboks captain, to the 42-man squad for the November Nations Championship matches, dropping Bordeaux's Nicolas Depoortere to make room. Ward cannot be eligible for France until next year under World Rugby's five-year residency rules, so his inclusion is purely for training purposes. The squad is hit by injuries: Jalibert, Ramos, Marchand, Meafou, Flament, Bamba and Nouchi are all ruled out.

lead.why: The Alldritt recall is already run, but the Ward call-up and the injury list are a separate, fresh squad angle for France.

teams.heading: Farrell calls up uncapped McNabney and Benson; Jack Conan ruled out
teams.body: Andy Farrell has called up two uncapped Ulster players, James McNabney and Jamie Benson, to the 36-man Ireland squad for the November Nations Championship games, with Jack Conan ruled out by a shoulder injury he picked up in Leinster's 48-23 win at Clermont Auvergne. McNabney (23) returns from an ACL injury that cost him the 2025/26 campaign, while Benson, who joined from Harlequins this summer, can play centre, out-half or full-back. "It's always great to give people a chance for the first time," Farrell said.

teams.body: The Scotsman reports that Scotland's Nations Championship squad has unprecedented depth, a situation that could lead to multiple big-name omissions. Scotland's most recent match was a 33-17 win over Fiji in Round three, and the next assignment is New Zealand in Round four.

teams.heading: Wales's Taulupe Faletau sidelined again by finger injury, misses Ospreys derby
teams.body: Wales number eight Taulupe Faletau is sidelined again: he will have surgery on a finger injury that flared after his Cardiff comeback. He will miss Cardiff's URC derby at Ospreys, and it is hoped he will be fit after the November break. Faletau was left out of Steve Tandy's Nations Championship squad, and Tandy has not ruled out a Wales return but wants him to show durability.

teams.heading: Ireland's Sam Prendergast injury scare still unresolved before Argentina clash
teams.body: Ireland's fly-half picture for the clash with Argentina remains unresolved. The Sun reports Ireland have been dealt a major injury scare, with Sam Prendergast described as likely to be tight for the match. A separate piece, headlined around his absence from a Munster game, presents the wrist problem as the start of a busy international window. For Argentina, the key point is that Prendergast is still on the fitness list, and no ruling has been reported either way.

teams.heading: Taniela Tupou and Tom Hooper missed Bledisloe Tests against the All Blacks
teams.body: Australia were without Taniela Tupou and Tom Hooper for the Bledisloe Cup defeats to New Zealand, because the All Blacks fixtures fell outside World Rugby's global player release period. The pair had played crucial bench roles in the win over back-to-back World Cup champions South Africa, and they play club rugby in France and England respectively. Both are in Les Kiss' 33-man spring tour squad for the November Tests.

teams.heading: Cheslin Kolbe says final Japan spell was 'worst feeling' away from family
teams.body: Cheslin Kolbe has described his final stint in Japan as the most challenging of his time abroad, with his wife and children staying in South Africa for the season. The Springbok winger joined Suntory Sungoliath after the 2023 World Cup and played three years for them before agreeing a deal to return to the Stormers. He told the For the Love of Rugby podcast he has no regrets about nine years abroad. His Stormers debut has been delayed by a broken jaw suffered on Springbok duty.

teams.heading: Captain Ardie Savea among seven more All Blacks unavailable for Nations Championship
teams.body: Captain Ardie Savea is among seven All Blacks listed as unavailable for next month’s Nations Championship campaign in Europe. Ruben Love (ankle), Luke Jacobson (elbow), Caleb Clarke (shoulder), Billy Proctor (shoulder), Ollie Norris (knee) and Tamaiti Williams (back) are also unavailable. They follow wing Leroy Carter, ruled out after ankle surgery for a hip-drop tackle in the first Bledisloe Cup Test in Auckland, and join Shannon Frizell, Tyrel Lomax and Samisoni Taukei’aho. Flyhalf Richie Mo’unga has not yet been ruled out.

lead.why: The only shortlisted Test-squad item, and it adds the wider unavailable list to the Sunday headline already run.

teams.heading: Springbok Andre Esterhuizen injured after 52 seconds as Sharks win at Cardiff
teams.body: Sharks captain and Springbok Andre Esterhuizen was forced off with a foot injury after just 52 seconds of Friday's United Rugby Championship win at Cardiff. Ethan Hooker scored in the second minute, and the visitors finished 36-21 winners with a bonus point, Hooker and Jurenzo Julius covering the midfield. Julius was replaced by Siya Masuku at half-time. The severity of the injury has not been reported.
